title: Anti-Steer Subgroups x Fairness: Does Safety Steering Protect Some Demographic Inputs Less Than Others?

original_idea.body: Using matched demographic-varying harmful templates, test whether a safety steering vector reduces harmful outputs unevenly across groups.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Fairness/disparate-protection is an ethics concern but the chain to catastrophic risk from advanced AI is vague.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Template-based prompts, steering, per-group rates, simple statistics; very accessible to a beginner.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped: matched templates, measure per-group protection disparity with significance test.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Template-based, synthetic, no internal access; equity-of-safety is externally doable and lab-deprioritized.

low_compute.reasoning: Pure inference on templates; CPU/free-tier feasible for small models.

novelty.reasoning: Demographic disparity in steering-based protection appears largely unexplored.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Combining anti-steerable heterogeneity with demographic fairness of safety protection is an underexplored angle.
